fields.detail: Directive 3: gsplit_line.py tested only ONE bipartition (even- vs odd-index blocks) and found it not strictly line-separable — a dead guess, not an obstruction. The question that bears on the induction f(n) <= 2*f(n-1): does ANY line (containing no point) split the verified es_construct set into two halves each free of a convex (n-1)-gon? Decide exhaustively at n=5,6,7. Method: every combinatorially distinct half-plane bipartition of a finite planar set is realized by a line through a pair of points (standard k-set fact), so enumerate the C(N,2) point pairs, the line through each pair, and the 4 perturbations assigning the two on-line points to either side — that covers every bipartition. For each: both sides must have exactly 2^{n-3} points and no convex (n-1)-subset (exact es_geom oracle, integer determinants). Report the exact count of distinct bipartitions tried and of valid splits, and state what an empty result rules out. If no line exists, record the negative in CONTEXT.md under Ruled out with scope exactly 'this es_construct realization at n=5,6,7', NOT all extremal sets, and update the G-split-consistent gap in research/backward/extremal-split-stability.md. Starter: code/out/gsplit_exhaustive.py — verify its bipartition enumeration is exhaustive before trusting its output.

The checker passed its self-test on hand-known sets — circle k=4..16 -> k, parabola, triangle+interior -> 3, square -> 4 (code/out/checker_vs_construction_resolution.md). This reproduces the ES(4)=5 / ES(5)=9 lower-bound witnesses (es_construct(4): 4 pts, largest convex 3 = no convex quad; es_construct(5): 8 pts, largest convex 4 = no convex pentagon) and the construction's n-gon emptiness at n=5,6. Scorer: takes a candidate module path on argv; module exposes points(k) returning integer (x,y) pairs. Constraints: under ten seconds per candidate (C(32,7)=3.4M subsets, so prune by convex-hull layers, not blind enumeration); memory bounded (8 GiB cap — a scorer that allocates without limit kills the run, not just the candidate).
